name: Lateral spinothalamic tract
summary: Small myelinated and unmyelinated pain and temperature fibers end in the dorsal horn (laminae I, II and V) within a segment or two of their entry; second-order neurons cross in the anterior white commissure over one to two segments and ascend in the anterolateral funiculus as the spinothalamic tract, joined in the brainstem by spinoreticular and spinomesencephalic fibers, to the ventral posterolateral thalamus and then the somatosensory cortex and insula. The early crossing is the key: cord lesions cause contralateral loss beginning one or two segments below the lesion, and a central cord lesion catches the crossing fibers of both sides for a band of dissociated loss.

origin.note: Free nerve endings (nociceptors and thermoreceptors); A-delta and C fibers; cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglia; second-order cells in the dorsal horn.

neuronChain.synapse: dorsal horn laminae I, II and V (via Lissauer's tract)
VPL thalamus (also intralaminar nuclei and reticular formation)

decussation.level: Anterior white commissure, 1–2 segments above entry
decussation.note: Second-order axons cross obliquely; a syrinx damages them here.

waypoints.note: synapse in the substantia gelatinosa and nucleus proprius
crosses in the anterior white commissure; ascends in the anterolateral funiculus, sacral fibers lateral
lateral medulla, dorsal to the olive

with projections to the insula and cingulate for the affective dimension of pain

termination: Ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus (discriminative pain), intralaminar nuclei and reticular formation (arousal and affect), periaqueductal gray (descending modulation).

lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Loss in the nerve or dermatome distribution, often with pain
Bilateral cape-like dissociated loss of pain and temperature at the involved segments with preserved touch and vibration
Contralateral loss starting one to two segments below the lesion
Contralateral body loss with ipsilateral facial loss (spinal trigeminal tract)
Contralateral hemianalgesia of face and body
Contralateral loss of all modalities, later central pain

pearls: Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side to weakness and proprioceptive loss is the hemicord
The sensory level for pin-prick is one to two segments below the true lesion
Sacral sparing means an intramedullary lesion: the sacral fibers lie most laterally

somatotopy: Cord: sacral fibers lateral and superficial, cervical medial (the reverse of the posterior columns). Brainstem: leg lateral, arm medial.
